newsitem.title: FINLAND: Enso says pulp price not to rise soon.
newsitem.headline: Enso says pulp price not to rise soon.

text.p: Finnish forest industry group Enso Oy's chief executive, Jukka Harmala, said on Monday that a good part of this year would pass before the price of pulp turned into a rise.
"I don't believe in a (pulp price) collapse, but quite a good part of the year will pass before the trend turns into a rise," Harmala told a news conference on Enso's 1996 results.
"Capacity utilisation rates are clearly on the rise," he said without specifying products. "We are on our way towards somewhat better markets," he added.
Harmala saw improving prospects for some product categories.
"I would imagine that newsprint (prices) would be better in the latter part of the year," he said.
"The first attempts to raise prices are underway in wood-containing newsprint and light-weight coated (LWC) products, the publication papers," Harmala said.
He expected the situation for liquid packaging board to remain quite stable.
Enso earlier reported a 53 percent fall in profit after financial items in 1996 to 1.67 billion markka from 3.52 billion the previous year. Net sales fell to 25.7 billion markka from 28.0 billion.
Looking ahead at 1997, Enso said in a statement: "The result for the year as a whole is expected to be about the same as in 1996."
"Enso expects its sales volumes to be higher than last year, but prices will improve only slowly from their present low levels," it added.
